summary: Same Voronoi pattern with an exactly matching palette and point-count mapping, but the port animates roughly 15x too slowly at every Speed setting, never fully stops at Speed=0, exposes only 4 of the original's 6 drawing modes and 4 of its 6 distance metrics (one of which renders as broken high-frequency confetti), and sits in a different drawing mode at untouched defaults.
observations: Rig is a 16x16 grid (256 px). Both sides compile and run clean (no compileError/runtimeError), neither binds sensors, and both stay alive and steady over a 240 s survey and a --skip 180 late window (brightnessTrend 'steady' on both, no decay, no freeze).

Untouched baseline (6 s, 20 fps): orig meanBrightness 125 / motion 17; port meanBrightness 62 / motion 1. The brightness gap is a MODE difference, not a dimming bug — see the untouched-default finding below.

Control surface: both sides expose exactly 4 sliders, but three of four NAMES/labels differ. orig sliderNumberOfPoints (NumberOfPoints) / sliderDistanceMethod (DistanceMethod) / sliderDrawingMode (DrawingMode) / sliderSpeed (Speed); port sliderPoints (Points) / sliderMetric (Metric) / sliderStyle (Style) / sliderSpeed (Speed). Kinds and count match; only Speed shares a name.

PALETTE IS AN EXACT MATCH. With the drawing mode forced flat and Points/Metric untouched (label vj-styonly-0.1), a dumped frame on each side contains exactly the same five RGB values: (0,255,101), (0,102,255), (203,0,255), (204,255,0), (255,0,0) — five cells on each side, differing only in which region each hue occupies.

UNTOUCHED DEFAULT DRAWING MODE DIFFERS. Dumping t=0 untouched and byte-comparing against runs that set only the mode dial: the original's untouched render is byte-identical to DrawingMode=0.1 (bucket 0 = flat, fully saturated cell fill), while the port's untouched render is byte-identical to Style=0.4 (bucket 1 = hue per cell with a brightness peak at the seed and dark cell edges). That is why the untouched sheets look different: orig = poster-flat colour blocks, port = shaded blobs.

SPEED: the port is ~15x too slow, at every Speed value. Measured by whole-frame decorrelation (corr of frame(0) vs frame(t), Style/DrawingMode=0.7, Metric/DistanceMethod=0, 10 fps, 20 s window), time to reach corr ~0.3 — Speed 0.25: orig ~0.65 s vs port ~9 s; Speed 0.5: orig ~0.35 s vs port ~6 s; Speed 0.75: orig ~0.2 s vs port ~3.2 s; Speed 1: orig ~0.2 s vs port ~3.2 s. Ratio ~14-17x throughout.

The Speed dial CANNOT compensate: the port at Speed=1 (decorrelation ~3.2 s) is still ~5x slower than the original at its slowest non-zero setting Speed=0.25 (~0.65 s). Motion stat at 20 fps over the same sweep: orig 0/11/20/30/37 at Speed 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1; port 0/1/2/2/3.

SPEED=0 DIVERGES: with Speed=0 the original is completely frozen (corr(frame0, frame(19 s)) = 1.00, motion 0 on every frame), but the port keeps drifting — corr falls to 0.92 at 6.4 s and 0.55 at 19 s. The port has a residual motion floor that the dial cannot switch off.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING DIFFERS. Rendering the same settings at 10/20/40 fps and reading decorrelation in SECONDS: the original hits corr 0.26 at 0.4 s / 0.2 s / 0.1 s respectively — i.e. a constant 4 FRAMES — so the original is frame-stepped, its speed scaling with fps. The port's curve is identical in seconds at 20 and 40 fps (0.87 @ 0.8 s, 0.68 @ 1.6 s, 0.26 @ 3.2 s) so it is time-based there, but at 10 fps it is exactly half speed in seconds while matching the 20 fps curve in frames — consistent with the port clamping its per-frame time step at ~0.05 s. Two different time models.

DRAWING MODE COUNT: hash-clustering a fixed-time dump across the dial in 0.05 steps (Points=0.5, Metric=0, Speed=0.5) gives the ORIGINAL six distinct looks — [0-0.20] flat saturated fill; [0.25-0.40] hue-per-cell with a bright seed and dark edges; [0.45-0.55] DIM rainbow rings (dark at the seed, colour in the mid-radius); [0.60-0.75] bright rainbow rings; [0.80-0.95] dark edge-glow (only cell borders lit); [1.00] soft wide rainbow blobs. The PORT gives only four — [0-0.25] flat fill; [0.30-0.50] bright-seed gradient; [0.55-0.75] bright rainbow rings; [0.80-1.00] edge glow.

Consequence of the mode gap: the port has no equivalent of the original's dim/inverted rainbow-ring mode or its soft-blob mode, and because the bucket boundaries differ the same slider value can land the two sides in different looks — at 0.5 the original draws dim rings while the port draws the bright-seed gradient; at 1.0 the original draws soft rainbow blobs while the port draws edge glow.

The four modes the port does have are good matches for their original counterparts: at 0.1 both draw flat saturated cells; at 0.3 both draw bright-seed gradients; at 0.7 both draw bright concentric rainbow rings with matching ring frequency; at 0.9 both draw near-black frames with only the cell borders faintly lit (orig mean 4, port mean 5).

DISTANCE METRIC COUNT: same experiment on the metric dial (Points=0.8, DrawingMode/Style=0, Speed=0.5, 0.05 steps) gives the ORIGINAL six distinct partitions (bucket edges between 0.20/0.25, 0.40/0.45, 0.55/0.60, 0.75/0.80, 0.95/1.00) and the PORT only four (edges between 0.25/0.30, 0.50/0.55, 0.75/0.80).

PORT METRIC BUCKET 2 IS BROKEN. At Metric in [0.30, 0.50] with the flat drawing mode the port renders per-pixel confetti on the 16x16 grid — no coherent Voronoi cells at all — while the original at the same slider value renders a clean partition with curved, lens-shaped cell boundaries. Re-rendered at 48x48 the port's output resolves into dense high-frequency concentric interference rings (a distance value wrapping many times per cell), confirming it is a genuinely wrong metric and not a 16x16 aliasing artefact.
Metric extremes match in character: at 0 both draw circular (Euclidean) rings; at 1.0 both draw the same diagonal-banded (Chebyshev/Manhattan-flavoured) partition.
POINT COUNT IS AN EXACT MATCH. Counting distinct flat-fill colours in a dumped frame across the points dial at 0/0.2/0.4/0.6/0.8/1: orig 1/2/3/5/6/8 and port 1/2/3/5/6/8 — identical at every setting.

RESOLUTION INDEPENDENCE MATCHES. Re-rendered at --grid 8x8 and --grid 48x48 with matched dials, both sides draw into the same logical canvas: same number of cells, same ring counts per cell, just coarser or finer. Neither side rasterises at native grid resolution.

Seed sweep (1, 7, 1234, untouched defaults): both sides respond to the seed with different point layouts; the port's slowness and mode/brightness offsets are unchanged, so none of the findings are a one-seed fluke.

dials.name: sliderNumberOfPoints (orig) / sliderPoints (port)
dials.origEffect: Sets the number of Voronoi seeds; distinct flat-fill colours counted 1/2/3/5/6/8 at slider 0/0.2/0.4/0.6/0.8/1.
dials.portEffect: Identical: 1/2/3/5/6/8 at the same slider values.

dials.name: sliderDistanceMethod (orig) / sliderMetric (port)
dials.origEffect: Six distinct distance metrics across the range (bucket edges ~0.22 / 0.42 / 0.57 / 0.77 / 0.97), from circular Euclidean cells at 0 through curved lens-shaped cells in the low-middle to diagonal-banded cells at 1.0. Every bucket yields a clean, coherent Voronoi partition.
dials.portEffect: Only four metrics (edges at 0.25-0.30 / 0.50-0.55 / 0.75-0.80). Bucket 0 (circular) and bucket 3 (diagonal bands) match the original's ends well. Bucket 2, slider 0.30-0.50, is broken — per-pixel confetti at 16x16, high-frequency concentric interference rings at 48x48, no cell structure.

dials.name: sliderDrawingMode (orig) / sliderStyle (port)
dials.origEffect: Six shading modes: flat saturated fill, bright-seed gradient, dim/inverted rainbow rings, bright rainbow rings, dark edge-glow, soft wide rainbow blobs. Untouched default sits in the flat-fill mode.
dials.portEffect: Four shading modes only: flat fill, bright-seed gradient, bright rainbow rings, edge glow. The dim-ring and soft-blob modes are absent, and the boundaries are on clean quarters so matched slider values land in different modes (0.5 and 1.0 in particular). Untouched default sits in the bright-seed gradient mode, not flat fill.

dials.name: sliderSpeed
dials.origEffect: Monotonic speed control, roughly linear (motion 0/11/20/30/37 at 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 at 20 fps); 0 freezes the pattern completely (corr 1.00 at a 19 s lag). Motion is frame-stepped: apparent speed scales with fps.
dials.portEffect: Same direction and monotonicity but ~15x slower at every setting (motion 0/1/2/2/3); the port at maximum speed is still ~5x slower than the original at its lowest non-zero setting. Speed=0 does not fully freeze — the port still drifts to corr 0.55 over 19 s. Motion is time-based above 20 fps with an apparent ~0.05 s per-frame step clamp below it.

feedback: Motion rate is the headline bug: the port needs roughly 15x more movement per unit time at every Speed setting. Measured by whole-frame decorrelation, the original reaches corr ~0.3 in 0.65 s / 0.35 s / 0.2 s / 0.2 s at Speed 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1; the port takes 9 s / 6 s / 3.2 s / 3.2 s. Scaling the port's seed-motion term by ~15 would land it on the original across the whole dial range.

The original's motion is FRAME-STEPPED (a fixed advance per rendered frame — its decorrelation lag is a constant 4 frames whether rendered at 10, 20 or 40 fps), whereas the port advances by elapsed time and additionally appears to clamp its per-frame step at ~0.05 s (10 fps runs half as fast in seconds as 20 fps runs). Match the original's per-frame stepping, or at minimum drop the step clamp so the port is at least consistently time-based.

Speed=0 must stop the pattern dead. The original is byte-frozen at Speed=0 (correlation 1.00 across a 19 s lag); the port still drifts (correlation 0.55 over the same lag). Something in the port's seed update is not multiplied by the speed term.

The Style/DrawingMode selector is missing two of the original's six shading modes. The original's six, in slider order, are: flat saturated per-cell fill; hue per cell with a brightness peak at the seed and dark edges; DIM rainbow rings that are dark at the seed with the colour band at mid radius; bright rainbow rings peaking at the seed; near-black edge-glow lighting only cell borders; and soft wide rainbow blobs with a smooth gaussian-like falloff. The port has only #1, #2, #4 and #5. Add the dim-ring and soft-blob modes and re-cut the boundaries into six equal buckets so the same slider value selects the same look on both sides (today the port's are quarters, so 0.5 and 1.0 land in different modes).

The Metric/DistanceMethod selector is missing two of the original's six metrics AND one of the four it has is broken. At slider 0.30-0.50 the port produces per-pixel confetti at 16x16 and dense concentric interference rings at 48x48 instead of a Voronoi partition — the distance value in that bucket is wrapping many times per cell (looks like a missing normalisation or an unbounded exponent). The original at the same value draws clean, curved lens-shaped cells. Fix that bucket, add the two missing metrics, and re-cut to six buckets.

Untouched-default drawing mode differs: the original's untouched render is byte-identical to DrawingMode=0.1 (flat saturated fill), the port's to Style=0.4 (bright-seed gradient). Initialise the port's style state to the flat-fill mode so the two agree with no dials touched — this alone accounts for the untouched mean-brightness gap of 125 vs 62.

Rename the port's controls to the original's names/labels so saved dial values and UI labels line up: sliderPoints -> sliderNumberOfPoints (NumberOfPoints), sliderMetric -> sliderDistanceMethod (DistanceMethod), sliderStyle -> sliderDrawingMode (DrawingMode). sliderSpeed already matches.

Do NOT change the palette, the point-count mapping, or the canvas mapping — all three are already exact: the same five RGB values appear on both sides, the visible cell count matches at every points setting (1/2/3/5/6/8), and both sides are resolution-independent at 8x8 and 48x48.
